public_rationale: The claim has an empirical part and a causal part. The evidence fits the empirical part read fairly. GPT-3 and InstructGPT kept making up information, at 41% and 21% on closed-domain tasks (e2). But fine-tuning without any grounding in the world halved that rate, which shows some capacity to reduce misinformation. TruthfulQA's authors tie false answers to imitating training text (e1), which partly fits Marcus's story. No cited study isolates the cause he names, being a model of word relations rather than of the world, from other factors. The causal part therefore stays open on the available evidence.
limitations: The evidence is about error rates, not about mechanism.
Settling this would need a controlled grounded-versus-ungrounded comparison, which no source here provides.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-3 cannot avoid producing misinformation because it models how words relate to each other, not how language relates to the world.

statement.excerpt: There is no intention to create misinformation—but also no capacity to avoid it, because fundamentally, GPT-3 is a model of how words relate to one another, not a model of how language might relate to the perceived world.

from_speaker: but also no capacity to avoid it
because fundamentally, GPT-3 is a model of how words relate to one another
not a model of how language might relate to the perceived world
our_interpretation: Two parts. (a) GPT-3 had no reliable built-in way to avoid producing false content. (b) The cause is that it is trained only on relations among words, without grounding in the perceived world.
Read fairly, 'no capacity to avoid it' means it cannot reliably avoid misinformation, not that it never says anything true.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evidence that GPT-3-era models' misinformation stems from text-only training, and that grounding in the world is what would be needed to fix it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that GPT-3-era models without world grounding could reliably avoid misinformation, or that the errors had a different main cause.
